title: Making Music with AI
content:
For the past month or so, I’ve been messing around with something new: making music with AI using Suno.com.

I’ve been playing with AI tools since before ChatGPT, but this is the first time I’ve really stepped into AI music. I’ve dabbled in audio tools like ElevenLabs for voice stuff, but not songwriting and production. Honestly, I wish I’d jumped in a year ago.

I named the project Parametra — a riff on parametric creation: output shaped by rules, inputs, and algorithms.

In design and math, “parametric” basically means: you set the parameters, and the system generates the results. That’s exactly what’s happening here. I bring the ideas, the emotions, bits of lyrics, a structure, a vibe. The AI interprets those parameters and turns them into sound.

So I’m not writing songs the old-school way with a notebook and a guitar. I’m building the “recipe” — pulling from journal notes, random thoughts, and whatever’s rattling around in my head — then seeing what happens when it gets translated into music.

A few weeks ago I released my first single, “On The Edge” — an 80s-leaning New Wave track. It’s up on Spotify now.

Today I uploaded my second single, “It’s Just My Nature” — more of an alt-country arrangement. It should hit Spotify, Apple Music, and the other platforms soon.

The wild part is hearing something that started as a half-formed thought turn into a song I’m replaying on my phone. Like vibe-coding, this is another AI use case that makes it feel like the future showed up early.

And yeah — I get it. A lot of people see this as an existential threat to artists. I understand that reaction. But I also feel like I’ve seen this movie before.

It reminds me of living through the shift from film to digital photography. We went from a smaller group of people being able to make great images to… basically everyone. Photography didn’t die. It evolved. We got more photos, more creators, more noise — and also more genuinely great work. Was it “better”? In some ways, yes. In other ways, it was messy. Evolution usually is.

I think music will follow a similar path — maybe even more personal, because music hits people in a different place. I’m curious to see where this goes, and how the definition of “creative” keeps changing.

title: Everything unfinished, together
content:
Introducing the new 1ThomasAlan.com

For years I’ve had my creative life split across too many sites—ShootLighter for photography, OneToBetter for ideas, ThePoeticAI for generative art and poetry, plus a handful of tech experiments parked on random domains.

It worked… but it also felt fragmented. Too many doors. Too many places to click.

So I’m simplifying.

Everything is coming home to one place: 1ThomasAlan.com.

This isn’t just a redesign. It’s me pulling the threads together—photography, AI art, writing, tech experiments, and now… music. Over the next few weeks I’ll be moving my portfolio over from ShootLighter.com, adding new pieces from The Poetic AI, and bringing in the small projects and notes that used to live across OneToBetter.com and other corners of the internet.

And for the first time, I’m adding music.

I just opened my DistroKid account and started releasing tracks I’ve been creating with Suno. They should hit Spotify and Apple Music within the week, and once they’re live, I’ll link them here—under the same umbrella as everything else I make.

One home for art, ideas, photos, sound, and technology.

It’s early. The paint is still drying. But it already feels better to have one address—one hub—where all of this can live together instead of scattered across the web.

I picked this MidJourney v7 image because it mirrors exactly what this site is right now: a creative workspace in the middle of becoming something.

More soon.
